Appendix B Subband Parameters

In this section we further discuss the intuition behind the mechanisms that drive the behaviour of the subband parameters in the main text. In particular we focus on the linear term α and β 2 . For the former, under the assumption of an infinite well and a 6-band Luttigner-Kohn model for the valence band, an analytic expression can be derived [ 6 ]

α = − 6 ​ 2 ​ α 0 ​ γ 3 ​ ℐ ​ { ⟨ f l | ​ k z ​ | f s ⟩ } (14)

with α 0 = ℏ 2 2 ​ m 0 a constant, γ 3 the Luttinger parameter, k z the momentum operator in the growth direction. Even though this expression strictly holds only for an infinite well, we can plot the main constituents for the heterostructure discussed in the main text to provide a physical intuition of the observed trends.

Fig. 5 reveals that the LH/SO overlap is strongly dependent on the thickness of the well and an increase in Ge concentration also boosts the Luttinger parameter γ 3 .
For the cubic Rashba β 2 we can again follow the intuition provided by the approximate expressions for an infinite QW. In particular, keeping only the second order terms in the perturbative expansion, and neglecting the split-off band contributions (effectively setting the f s = 0 ) [ 6 ]

β 2 = 3 ​ i ​ α 0 2 ​ ( γ 2 − γ 3 ) ​ γ 3 ​ ⟨ f 0 l | ​ [ k z , ∑ l | f l H ⟩ ​ ⟨ f l H | E 0 − E l ​ | f 0 l ⟩ ] (15)

where E 0 denotes the energy of the lowest Light-Hole subband and f H is the label of the Heavy-Hole subbands.

In Fig. 6 we observe the behavior of this expression and the resemblance with the trends observed in the main text. We note however that for both β 2 and β 3 the third order Schrieffer-Wolff terms are especially relevant and dominate the dynamics of β 3 with respect to the first and second order terms [ 36 ] .
